blocks.content: ETHAN
I didn't mean to draw her again.
For the record. Even though there's no record. Even though the only witness is the sketchbook, which isn't going to say anything either way.

My room: paint smell, cold coffee, laundry I'd meant to fold three days ago. My mom had left a note on the fridge — eat something that isn't coffee — which I read while drinking coffee. The house was quiet. Quiet enough for my thoughts to get loud, which is the problem with quiet.
The first sketch was only supposed to be the archway. Then the bench. Then the fountain. Then — somehow — a figure standing beside it.
Loose lines. The suggestion of red hair. A stuffed dinosaur I had apparently rendered with enough anatomical detail to suggest I'd been looking at it for a while.
I knew her name now. That made it worse. Names are handles. Once you have a handle on something, it's harder to put down.
I leaned back and pressed both hands over my face.
You talked to her for three minutes.
This is how people become embarrassing poems.

I looked at the sketch. As a painter I think in images, which means when I try to remember something I don't get words — I get a picture. Hers: the way she said most good things aren't like she was tossing a line into deep water and wasn't really watching to see if anything caught. The gap behind her eyes that lasted half a second before the brightness came back.
I darkened the archway. Softened her face. Left the eyes blank, the way I always do — eyes make drawings too honest.
My phone buzzed.
bro. alive or dramatically painting somewhere
both
concerning. did you eat
I looked at the empty coffee cup on my desk.
define eat
coming over tomorrow. you need adult supervision
we're the same age
spiritually i am your father
I smiled and set the phone down.
The painting was drying against the wall. I crossed the room and looked at it. The fountain was warmer than it had any right to be. Not fixed — just like the light had decided it was worth touching.
I picked up a small brush and added one thin line of gold along the water.
Hopeful, maybe. Dishonest, maybe. I've been told those aren't always different things.
